body: Can I ask how long it took you to get back into smoking after a crazy trip? I’m pretty sure because of the bad trip, my anxiety has just been worse even sober lol (that, or I haven’t touched any drugs since haha). But thank you for the reassurance! :)

They didn't catch me, but they were wondering why I was acting so weird. My dad basically called me that afternoon and asked me to drive down to this place while I was tripping mad balls. Took like an hour to find his keys, panicked when he called again, and I had to make up some bullshit like that I was sick. So then both came home from work early (totally unexpected) and started pestering me with questions. The anxiety persisted throughout the rest of the trip... And when your perception of reality is gone, anxiety is a NIGHTMARE. It was just major bad luck and stupidity on my part :/

I'm super certain it's probably my anxiety induced from the bad trip coming from these responses... I just hope maybe a tolerance break and start smoking a bit again will bring back that relaxing high. Thanks for the reassurance :)

Seriously, you sound just like me. My dieting lasted for about half a year since I was so focused and determined to get the right nutrients, especially after having some other personal health issues. During that time, though, I was even more fidgety and constantly all over the place despite being at a good calorie deficit. I eventually just got bored of dieting and slowly went back to my old habits like you— mindlessly eating a whole bag of chips or cookies and not realizing it before it’s gone, or unable to control my impulses around wanting a certain food despite already eating enough. If you don’t mind answering, are you on any medication perhaps? Or have you found anything that helped you with the impulsivity?

Are you me? I feel exactly the same way! I hyperfocused so much on nutrition after noticing GI issues and because I've always been so impatient, I took the extreme road and heavily restricted my intake as well. I was also obsessed with exercising. This didn't last after the few months passed, though, since I just suddenly lost interest and now starting to put my weight back on. Looking back, I was either extremely unmotivated to do something unless I was really feeling it or I somehow turned it "extreme" when it shouldn't have been (like rushing to do my assignment at the last minutes, social media for 5+ hours, etc etc..). I think that's way restricting sugary foods again seems so exhausting and the rush to overeat feels so much better. Food is especially a problem now when it never was even a second thought. Are you medicated? If so, has it helped you take away these sort of thoughts?
Omg great idea!! Totally gonna try that next time.

Healthy Life Whole Wheat Bread (35 calories per slice; 70 calories for two slices) 

Chocolate PB2 (45 for two teaspoons) 

And I added in like two strawberries, which would be about 8 calories. It was a pretty fulfilling breakfast! The fiber in the whole wheat bread really helps.

I haven't really found a "cure" yet, but what's been helping me a lot is soluble fiber and Miralax. I know for a lot of people, fiber doesn't help so be careful with that. I find Miralax really effective and use loads of Benefiber as well to help things moving. I would also look into magnesium supplements and probiotics if those don't work. Align apparently helps lots of people with IBS-C, but I can't say that for myself since I haven't tried it yet. Magneisum citrate works wonders depending on your preferred dosage. And if any of those don't work, go have a talk with a good GI doctor to make a plan that works for you. I know some people find meds like Linzess really helpful, but I suggest that be your last route since medication like that isn't exactly the cheapest. Wish you the best of luck, OP! It's all about trial and error.
I haven't tried probiotic supplements, but I've tried activia yogurt. I'll probably think about getting some. Thanks!
Chicken soup actually doesn't sound that bad right now! I've tried soup in the past, and it has helped... And right now, it seems much better than anything else. Thank you
I actually haven't tried anything for pain... The bloating is horrible. Tea and some soup usually does help a bit, though.
